html:
For me, fingerstyle doesn’t get better the faster, slicker and more explosive it is; it’s playing with feeling that draws me in. So I can’t really get into speed merchants like Tommy Emmanuel. I prefer lyrical players like Sungha Jung (though his hands are fast too), Masaaki Kishibe and Kotaro Oshio.

This really varies from person to person. I played some Sungha Jung for a colleague, and he said he couldn’t stand it; it made him want to sleep. He still prefers the explosive stuff.

Today on YouTube I discovered Chuxiao Yang and Yan Huang, two Chinese fingerstyle guitarists who have a lot in common with the last three players above. I love them. They’ve won me over.

Still, listen to or play too much of this style and it inevitably gets a bit samey. Lately I’ve fallen for the blues instead: that raw sense of rhythm and groove is irresistible.

PS: I now follow Jiazhuo Liu’s updates. He’s released lots of original pieces recently. He’s no longer mainly about speed, and he’s putting more and more of his own feeling into his technique.
